newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CPI MAY BE LESS THAN 13 PCT IN DECEMBER-PM.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CPI MAY BE LESS THAN 13 PCT IN DECEMBER-PM.

text.p: Judging on current performance, Poland's year-on-year consumer price inflation in December 1997 may be less than the 13 percent planned in the budget, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Thursday.

"Not only does it seem very realistic we can lower it to 13 percent in December, but it is not out of the question that, for the first time in history, we will manage to get a lower inflation rate than planned," he told Reuters in an interview.
"So far the situation has developed more favourably than we planned and in the first three months inflation was lower than prognosed by 1.3 percentage points, which is significant," Cimoszewicz said.
Year-on-year consumer price inflation in March was 16.6 percent down from 18.5 percent in December last year.
Cimoszewicz said the government, which faces general elections around September, would continue the policies that had ensured inflation remained under control.
He said that Poland's trade deficit, partly offset by a surplus in services and cross border trade, did not give cause for great concern and he saw no fundamental need to alter monetary policy.
"At this moment I see no dangerous phenomenon in our economy and therefore I look at what is happening with great optimism," Cimoszewicz said.
